purpose: Personal-investment research for metals and cross-commodity resource exposures relevant to electrification, data-centre infrastructure, food security and nuclear fuel.

ideas.name: BHP Group ADR
ideas.thesis: BHP remains the preferred diversified resource platform because copper is now its largest earnings engine while Jansen adds potash and Olympic Dam adds uranium by-product optionality.
ideas.catalysts: Sustained high copper prices, expansion at Escondida/Copper South Australia, Vicuña development decisions, Jansen potash production from 2027 and further Olympic Dam expansion work.
ideas.risks: Copper and iron-ore cyclicality, China/global growth exposure, Jansen execution, large-project capital discipline and valuation rerating after strong copper performance.
ideas.valuationTechnical: Copper has already rerated sharply, so prefer pullbacks and avoid capitalising flash-squeeze pricing as a permanent earnings base.
ideas.researchNote: The structural copper case strengthened again after the LME cash market experienced an extreme squeeze: cash copper briefly reached about $14,912/t and cash-to-three-month backwardation widened to $545/t as live LME stocks became scarce relative to concentrated long positions. The squeeze is partly positioning/arbitrage-driven, but it confirms a fragile physical buffer. BHP remains preferable to chasing pure spot beta at distressed backwardation extremes.

categoryRead: Copper remains the highest-priority metal for Power Stack, but current spot tightness has become unusually disorderly. The physical shortage signal supports grid, cable and electrical-equipment pricing power, while also raising input-cost risk for contractors and low-margin manufacturers. Aluminium has eased from its war premium as Chinese exports rise, and Chinese steel remains pressured by weak construction despite stronger auto/technology exports.

currentSignals.copper: Severely tight near-term physical market; flash squeeze and backwardation require valuation discipline.
currentSignals.aluminium: War-related tightness partly relieved by Chinese alloy/semi exports; less acute than copper.
currentSignals.steel: China construction demand remains weak; July output fell 3.6% y/y and inventories are elevated.
currentSignals.goldSilver: Precious metals remain supported by fiscal/inflation uncertainty and volatile long-end real rates; silver is higher beta and less core to Power Stack.
